subject: Not surveying a whole circle and having the area surveyed vary

messages.author: 467935df0dfab29b
messages.subject: Not surveying a whole circle and having the area surveyed vary
parts:
Greetings! My name is Matt McClanahan. I'm a graduate student at the Un=
iversity of Tennessee doing research on wintering waterfowl. I am still =
knee-deep in estimating duck densities among target habitat types and exp=
erimental management plots. I have 2 types of survey plots: (1) habitat =
sites, in which we did a modified point transect in continuous habitat ("=
half-circle"), and (2) bounded, rectangular experimental plots treated wi=
th disking and cover planting.

I have estimated densities with Distance, but the numbers are super low c=
ompared to what should've been there. Distance is estimating density usi=
ng a full circle, and I am not sure how to refine the densities such that=
they don't just conform to a half-circle, but rather I want the densitie=
s to be estimated using the actual area of my survey plots (which I estim=
ated using GIS). While I think I could readily use multipliers, I can't =
apply more than one sampling fraction within Distance; my survey plot siz=
es varied within habitat types.=20=20

I have tried using the following formula:

=E2=80=8BD(actual) =3D D(Distance) * [pi*w^2 / A(GIS)]

Where D(actual) is the refined density estimate, D(Distance) is the densi=
ty estimate from Distance (estimated using a full circle), pi*w^2 is the =
area of a circular plot with truncation distance w (in hectares), and A(G=
IS) is the area of the survey plot estimated with GIS (also estimated in =
hectares). The formula was used post hoc in Excel on each density estima=
te (weekly transect or sample). The idea was to create a "correction fac=
tor" by which I could multiply Distance's density estimate and get a much=
higher one that better reflected what was actually present within the su=
rvey plot. If I have lost anyone, just let me know. The formula seemed =
promising, but I don't know if I am way out in left field with this appro=
ach. Can anyone provide any advice or direction on the matter?
